This Town Adopted Trauma-Informed Care—And Saw a Decrease in Crime and Suspension Rates

http://www.yesmagazine.org/people-power/this-town-adopted-trauma-informed-care-and-saw-a-decrease-in-crime-and-suspension-rates-20170222

This is good news.

Jean Liedloff's book, The Continuum Concept, explained that human nature is to be happy, when people are raised in healthy families in healthy communities. I think her findings led to Attachment Parenting, which is important for infants to be healthy and free of trauma.

The alternative schools discussed in this article are schools where troubled youths were sent. They learned to help students discover their own traumas in order to find how best to deal with or overcome them. (Some of their practices are questionable, like giving students birth-control pills, partly because they tend to cause breast and uterine cancer, I believe, and some are more dangerous, like giving them access to Ibuprofen, which is a very dangerous drug.) But for the most part the trauma-informed care policy seems to be very healthy for students and society.

If schools become aware of causes of students' trauma, maybe they'll soon come to realize that many schooling practices are traumatic for most students. This is why I've been promoting unschooling and homeschooling for many years. Unschooling means un-brainwashing, un-badgering, un-threatening, self-directing learning.
